title: Roasted Broccoli with Tahini
subtitle: Charred broccoli with a lemony tahini dressing
excerpt: High-heat roasting transforms broccoli. The florets char at the edges and turn nutty. The tahini sauce is sharp with lemon and loosened with water to a pourable consistency. Toasted almonds add crunch.
sourceNotes: Roasted vegetables with tahini dressing are a cornerstone of modern Middle Eastern cooking. The combination became widely known in Britain and North America through the influence of Israeli and Palestinian food writers in the 2010s.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Roast the broccoli up to 2 hours ahead. The tahini dressing keeps refrigerated for a week.

content.text: Give the broccoli space in the tin. Crowded florets steam rather than char. Use two tins if needed.

items.prepNote: cut into large florets, stalks sliced

content.text: Toss the broccoli with the olive oil, chilli flakes, and a good pinch of salt.
Spread across one or two large roasting tins in a single layer.
Roast for 20 to 25 minutes until charred at the edges and tender.
While the broccoli roasts, make the tahini sauce. Whisk together the tahini, lemon juice, and garlic.
Add cold water a tablespoon at a time, whisking, until the sauce is pourable. Season with salt.
Arrange the roasted broccoli on a plate. Drizzle the tahini sauce over the top.
Scatter over the toasted almonds and parsley. Serve warm or at room temperature.

items.symptom: Broccoli is soft but not charred.
items.cause: Too much oil or tin too crowded.
items.fix: Spread further apart. Less oil gives more char.

items.symptom: Tahini sauce is very thick and pasty.
items.fix: Whisk in more water a little at a time until it pours easily.
Whisk vigorously. Add a drop more water and keep whisking.
